scope:
Voltage class along the PS3 mains lead's unsupported span (R43).

The span is the 315 mm of the J11 -> PS3 AC lead between its two tie points (T_J11 and T_AC, check_ps3_retention.py). Every STEP_MM along its centre
line (r43_world.centerline, the line that was built) the exact distance from the cable surface (centre-line distance less half the OD) to the nearest part of
each voltage class is taken, with the classes of the PS3 clearance check (evidence/ps3/check_ps3_clearances.cls: HOT = mains side, SELV, interface = native-21
J3/J4 mates, and 'other' = every unclassified part: enclosure, fasteners, PE conductors, structure) plus the WiFi coax as SELV (as check_ps3_retention).
The lead itself is skipped; nothing else is.

Droop rule (the brief): the span can sag by up to the headroom the retention check reports (the cable-surface clearance to the nearest solid along the
span, ps3-retention.json 'spacing'), in any direction (conservative: sag is really downward). A SELV part is "within 8 mm of where the span could sag"
when  (SELV clearance - headroom) < 8 mm, that is, SELV clearance < headroom + 8 mm. If that happens anywhere, R43 would add a mid-span support.
The cable's own stiffness is not modelled; the headroom is a clearance, not a sag prediction.

Run after src/assembly.py and check_ps3_retention.py: python evidence/ps3/survey_mains_span.py   (writes evidence/ps3/ps3-mains-span.json)
